references.text: Describes the arrival of the children of Israel in Egypt and their enslavement by the Egyptians, fulfilling the promise that Abraham's descendants would be strangers in a land not their own.
States that the stay of the children of Israel in Egypt lasted 430 years, closely linked to the 400 years mentioned in the promise to Abram.
God tells Jacob to go down to Egypt and that his descendants will become a great nation there, and that God will bring them back up again.
The psalmist recalls how Israel came to Egypt and became strangers there, and how the Egyptians turned against them—a reflection of the prophecy about slavery.
Stephen quotes directly from God's words to Abraham that his descendants would live as strangers in a foreign land and be oppressed for 400 years.
Paul mentions that God chose Israel's fathers and exalted the people during their stay in Egypt, and then brought them out of there.
Direct quote and confirmation of the prophecy about 400 years of being strangers and oppression.
